issues.title: Host check is case-sensitive after dict() copy
issues.explanation: dict(self._orig.headers) drops the case-insensitive lookup, so a user header typed as `host:` is not seen by `'Host' not in headers` and a second Host line is added. The printed request then shows two Host headers while only the user's one is sent (issue #235).
issues.fix: Check the original CaseInsensitiveDict: if 'Host' not in self._orig.headers: headers['Host'] = ...
